brief: Goldman flags three forecast changes and ties them to one cause. Assuming Middle East shipping disruptions continue into 2027, the December 2026 and full-year 2027 Brent forecasts go to $85 and $80 per barrel from $80 and $75. Assuming a further delayed normalization of Persian Gulf LNG exports, the 4Q26 TTF gas forecast goes to 70 euros per MWh from 53. Higher energy prices then feed the policy call: the ECB forecast is revised to one more 25bp hike in December for a 2.75% peak versus 2.5% before, on energy prices plus recent resilience and hawkish September messaging, with a low hurdle for another. Globally, growth slows to 2.6% in 2026 on energy headwinds while core inflation ends the year at 2.8%. In the US, growth is 2.0% Q4/Q4 as subdued consumer spending is offset by the AI boom, core PCE is 3.0% in December before falling near 2% in 2027, unemployment ends at 4.2%, and the Fed holds 3.5-3.75% with persistent oil disruption tilting policy risk up. Euro area growth is 0.9%, China 4.6% on exports. The forecast table carries the S&P 500 at 8,000 and gold at $4,836.
